title: The p-vanishing partition classification conjecture for primes at least 5
statement:
Let $p$ be a prime and let $n$ be a nonnegative integer. A partition of $n$ is **$p$-vanishing** if every irreducible character of $S_n$ whose degree is divisible by $p$ vanishes on the corresponding conjugacy class. A partition is of **$p$-adic type** if it has the form

$$
(f_{k,1}p^k,\ldots,f_{k,h_k}p^k,\ldots,f_{0,1},\ldots,f_{0,h_0})
$$

where $(f_{i,1},\ldots,f_{i,h_i})\vdash a_i$ for $0\leq i\leq k$ and $0\leq a_i<p$.

**The p-vanishing partition classification conjecture.** If $p\geq 5$, then a partition is $p$-vanishing if and only if it is of $p$-adic type.

Partitions of $p$-adic type are known to be $p$-vanishing, while examples for $p=2$ and $p=3$ show that the equivalence fails for those primes. The conjecture asserts that no additional $p$-vanishing partitions occur for primes at least $5$.
source_name: Lucia Morotti, “p-vanishing conjugacy classes of symmetric groups”, arXiv:1409.8108 (2015).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1409.8108

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2014).
